title: Temperature Next-Token Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI for EE Research
description: Prediction activity in which learners infer whether the probability of the top-ranked or lowest-ranked of five illustrative candidate next tokens rises, falls, or stays the same when the sampling temperature changes, then reveal the softmax distribution computed from the formula. Three predictions in a fixed order allow one attempt each; an exploration mode then offers a temperature slider from 0.1 to 2.0 and a reproducible Draw 10 Samples button with a fixed seed of 42.

educational.topic: Temperature and sampling in language models
learningObjectives: Infer, before it is revealed, whether the probability of the top-ranked and of the lowest-ranked candidate token rises or falls when the temperature is raised or lowered
prerequisites: Temperature with the formula p_i = exp(z_i/T) / sum_j exp(z_j/T)

accessibility.notes: describe() provides a screen-reader description; all controls are native HTML elements (buttons, select lists, text input, range sliders) reachable with the Tab key; correct and incorrect feedback uses words and symbols as well as color; colors come from the Okabe-Ito color-blind-safe palette; body text is 15 px or larger.

controls.label: rises / falls / stays the same
controls.purpose: Learner's committed prediction for the current item.

controls.label: Reveal
controls.purpose: Commits the prediction (one attempt), changes the chart to the new temperature, and shows feedback.

controls.label: Next Prediction / Open Exploration Mode
controls.purpose: Enabled after a reveal; poses the next prediction from temperature 1.0, and after prediction 3 opens exploration mode.

controls.label: Temperature
controls.purpose: Exploration mode: temperature from 0.1 to 2.0 in steps of 0.1 (default 1.0).

controls.label: Draw 10 Samples
controls.purpose: Exploration mode: draws ten synthetic samples at the current temperature with a fixed seed of 42 and counts how many are the top token.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-reveal with committed predictions, followed by free exploration and reproducible sampling
keyQuestions: If temperature drops to 0.5, what happens to the probability of the top token?
Does temperature change which token ranks first?
Why does a lower temperature make output more repeatable but not more correct?
commonMisconceptions: Low temperature makes the model more accurate
Temperature changes which token ranks first
At high temperature every token becomes equally likely
assessmentOpportunities: Mastery is 3 of 3 predictions correct, each committed before the distribution is revealed
Dragging the temperature control freely is exploration and is not evidence of mastery
